experiment.say: do an experiment · a science experiment

sergeant.say: a police sergeant · an army sergeant
ex: My brother is a sergeant in the army.
The police sergeant asked for my name.
Is the sergeant here today?
The sergeant gives orders to the soldiers.

pilot.say: an airline pilot · fly a plane
ex: My uncle is a pilot.
Do you want to be a pilot?
The pilot says we land in ten minutes.
The pilot landed the plane safely.

welcome.note: Also a verb: "They welcomed us." Answer "Thank you" with "You're welcome."

congress.say: in Congress · a member of Congress
ex: Congress passed a new law today.
What does Congress do in the US?
She works for a member of Congress.
Doctors from many countries came to the congress.
congress.note: In the US, written with a capital C and no "the": Congress.

professional.say: ask a professional · a health professional
professional.note: Most often an adjective: "a professional team", "get professional help".

ex: Eye color is in our genes.
She got her height from her dad's genes.
Some illnesses come from one bad gene.
Do you think good health is in the genes?

institute.say: at an institute · a research institute
ex: She studies at a technical institute.
He works at a research institute.
Where is the art institute?
The institute is near the city center.
institute.note: To talk about studies, Americans usually say "college" or "university".

ex: That's complete nonsense!
Stop talking nonsense, please.
This article is full of nonsense.
Don't believe that nonsense about the test.
This movie is about a demon.
Do you believe in demons?
In the story, a demon lives in the forest.
My son draws demons with red eyes.

ID.say: show your ID · a photo ID
ID.note: Say each letter: "eye-dee". It means an identity card or document.

face.say: wash your face · on your face

ex: Islam is a big world religion.
What do you know about Islam?
She studies the history of Islam.
Ramadan is a holy month in Islam.
Islam.note: Always with a capital I and no "the": Islam.

sheriff.note: In the US, a sheriff is the elected head of police in a county.

record.say: break a record · set a record · a world record
ex: She broke the world record.
What is the world record for this?
He has the school record for running.
This is a new record for our team.
record.note: Most often "record" means saved facts or sound: "medical records", "record a video".

IT.say: work in IT · the IT department
IT.note: Say each letter: "eye-tee". It is not the word "it".

rock.say: a rock band · rock music · a rock concert
ex: Do you like rock or jazz?
My dad plays in a rock band.
This is a classic rock song.
Let's go to a rock concert on Friday.
rock.note: Most often "rock" means a stone: "He sat on a big rock."

robot.say: a toy robot · a robot vacuum
ex: Our robot cleans the floor every day.
Robots build cars in this factory.
Can I buy a toy robot here?
My son wants a robot for his birthday.

live.say: live music · play live · watch live
ex: Is there live music here tonight?
The band plays live on Fridays.
We watched a live concert on TV.
This show is live, not recorded.
live.note: This "live" sounds like "five". The verb "live" (sounds like "give") means to have a home.

journalist.say: work as a journalist · a sports journalist
ex: She works as a journalist for a newspaper.
A journalist asked me some questions.
He wants to be a sports journalist.
Are you a journalist?

producer.say: a music producer · a TV producer
ex: He is a music producer.
She works as a TV producer.
The producer likes our song.
Who is the producer of this film?
producer.note: Also a company or country that makes goods: "a big oil producer".

vice president.say: vice president of sales · the Vice President
ex: The vice president met with the workers.
She is vice president of sales.
Who is the vice president of the company?
He became vice president last year.

hip-hop.say: listen to hip-hop · a hip-hop artist
ex: My son listens to hip-hop every day.
Do you like hip-hop or rock?
There is a free hip-hop concert tonight.
She takes a hip-hop dance class.

virus.say: have a virus · a computer virus

user.say: a new user · a user name

device.say: charge a device · on any device
device.note: Also any tool made for a job: "a safety device".

stress.say: a lot of stress · under stress · stress at work
ex: I have a lot of stress at work.
Exercise helps with stress.
What helps you with stress?
Exams cause a lot of stress.
stress.note: Usually uncountable: "a lot of stress," not "many stresses."

ex: The news was a big shock.
It was a shock to see him here.
He was in shock after the accident.
Is she still in shock?

cap.say: wear a cap · a baseball cap
ex: Put on your cap, it's sunny.
Where did you buy that cap?
He wears a baseball cap every day.
I like your new cap.
cap.note: Also the top of a bottle or pen: "Where is the cap for this pen?"

gas.say: a gas stove · turn off the gas
gas.note: In American English "gas" also often means fuel for a car (gasoline).

highway.say: on the highway · take the highway

hit.say: a big hit · a hit song
ex: This song is a big hit.
What's this summer's biggest hit?
The band had many hits in the 90s.
The DJ plays old hits all night.
hit.note: Most often "hit" is a verb: "Don't hit your sister."

stand.say: visit our stand · at the stand
stand.note: Most often a verb: "Please stand here." At a fair, Americans often say "booth".

nerve.say: nerve damage · a nerve in your back
ex: The doctor says a nerve is damaged.
I have pain in a nerve in my back.
Can the dentist save the nerve in my tooth?
Nerves carry signals to the brain.
nerve.note: "Have the nerve to" means to be brave or rude enough: "He had the nerve to ask."

sandwich.say: a ham sandwich · make a sandwich

sector.say: the public sector · in the tech sector
ex: She works in the public sector.
The tech sector is growing fast.
Many jobs are in the service sector.
Which sector do you work in?

tunnel.say: through a tunnel · in the tunnel
ex: The train goes through a long tunnel.
There is a lot of traffic in the tunnel.
Is there a tunnel under the river?
The tunnel connects two parts of the city.
Police caught two terrorists at the airport.
The terrorists are in prison now.
Do the police know who the terrorists are?
Police stopped a terrorist attack last week.
Look at the ice crystals on the window.
Salt and sugar are made of crystals.
Can we grow crystals at home?
She grew crystals in science class.

loser.say: feel like a loser · a total loser
ex: He called his brother a loser.
Don't feel like a loser after one mistake.
Why do you think you are a loser?
In the movie, he is a loser with no job.
loser.note: Rude when used about a person. It also means the one who loses a game.

duke.say: the Duke of ... · a duke and duchess
ex: The duke lives in a big castle.
The duke and duchess visit the city today.
Is he a real duke?
He became a duke when his father died.

dealer.say: a car dealer · buy from a dealer

era.say: the end of an era · in the era of
ex: The internet started a new era.
This song is from the disco era.
We live in the era of smartphones.
Which era of history do you like most?
There is live entertainment at the hotel.
Is there any entertainment for kids here?
TV is his only entertainment.
She works in the entertainment business.

medal.say: win a medal · a gold medal
ex: She won a gold medal.
Can I see your medal?
Our team got a silver medal.
Every runner gets a medal at the end.

aspect.say: every aspect of · an important aspect
ex: Money is an important aspect of the job.
I like every aspect of my new job.
What aspect of the work do you like most?
The best aspect of the hotel is the view.

soup.say: a bowl of soup · chicken soup

ex: My daughter is working on a photo project for school.
Can I use your pictures for my photo project?
Her photo project shows old buildings in Kyiv.
The museum has a new photo project about the city.
My grandmother listens to a radio drama every evening.
Do you know any good radio dramas for kids?
The actors record the radio drama in a small studio.
A radio drama tells a story with only voices and sounds.

business client.say: a new business client · for business clients
ex: The bank has special accounts for business clients.
Can business clients pay by bank transfer?
She meets with a business client every Monday morning.
We offer free delivery for all business clients.
business client.note: "Business customer" and "corporate client" are also common.

auto show.say: at the auto show · go to an auto show
ex: We saw many new electric cars at the auto show.
When does the auto show open this year?
The auto show is in a big hall downtown.
My son wants to go to the auto show with me.

auto center.say: take your car to the auto center
ex: Take your car to the auto center for an oil change.
Is the auto center open on Sundays?
The auto center fixed my brakes in one hour.
There is a big auto center near the highway.
auto center.note: In the US, usually a place that repairs cars, often inside a big store.

solo artist.say: become a solo artist · go solo
ex: After the band broke up, she became a solo artist.
He is a famous solo artist now.
Is she in a band or a solo artist?
This solo artist writes all her own songs.

senate.say: in the Senate · a seat in the Senate
senate.note: Usually written with a capital S: the Senate.

garage.say: in the garage · a garage sale
ex: He parks the car in the garage every night.
Our garage is full of old boxes.
Can you close the garage door, please?
They turned the garage into a small gym.

software.note: Uncountable: say "some software," not "a software" or "softwares."
